questionText:
Pick up the most effective word from the given words to fill in the blanks to make the sentence meaningfully complete.

According to the weather ________ it is going to be cloudy today.
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is option 4) i.e. Forecast.

Explanation

  • Let us explore the options:
    • 'Announcement' means a public notification or declaration.
    • 'Indication' means something that is indicated as advisable or necessary.
    • 'Prediction' means something that is predicted.
    • 'Forecast' means to calculate or predict (some future event or condition) usually as a result of study and analysis of available pertinent data, especially: to predict (weather conditions) on the basis of correlated meteorological observations.
  • Hence, from the explanation of the given options, we can easily say that 'forecast' is the correct answer.

The correct sentence: "According to the weather forecast it is going to be cloudy today."

  • Weather forecasting is the application of science and technology to predict the conditions of the atmosphere for a given location and time.
  • Weather warnings are important forecasts because they are used to protect life and property.
  • Examples of 'forecast' in a sentence:
    • "The weather forecast is predicting more rain."
    • "The weather forecast is good; there will be no delays."

questionText:
Direction: Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

There are actually many different versions of "Cinderella."
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is "Variations."

Key Points

  • "Version" means a thing which has the same basic contents as something else but which is presented in a different way. ((किसी वस्‍तु का) रूपांतर (मूल से भिन्‍न रूप में प्रस्‍तुति यद्यपि अंतर्वस्तु वही))
    • Example: Have you heard the live version of this song?
  • Synonym of "versions" is "variations."
  • "Variations" means different forms or versions of something. (किसी वस्‍तु की मात्रा या स्‍तर में परिवर्तन या भिन्‍नता, परिवर्तन या भिन्‍नता की मात्रा या स्‍तर)
    • Example: There are many variations of the classic fairy tale "Cinderella".
  • The correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

  • Problems: a thing that is difficult to deal with or to understand. (समस्‍या, मसला जिससे निपटना या जिसे समझना कठिन हो)
  • Features: an important or noticeable part of something. ((किसी का) महत्वपूर्ण या उल्‍लेखनीय भाग)
  • Signals: a sign, action or sound that sends a particular message. (विशेष संदेश देने वाला चिह्न, कार्य या ध्‍वनि; संकेत)

questionText:
Direction: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

The rabbit was chased (A) by the dog (B) into the forest dense. (C) No error (D)
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is 'Option 3' (C).

Key Points

  • The error in this sentence lies in the phrase indicated by 'C' ("into the forest dense").
  • The phrase "forest dense" is improperly ordered according to English syntax.
  • The correct order should be "dense forest", which would make the corrected sentence: "The rabbit was chased by the dog into the dense forest."
  • This type of error is related to the incorrect placement of adjectives in a sentence. Adjectives commonly precede the noun they modify.

Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 3' (C).

Additional Information

  • Option 1 (A) 'The rabbit was chased' is free from any errors as it correctly uses the passive voice in a past tense context.
  • Option 2 (B) 'by the dog' is grammatically correct. It correctly shows the agent of the action in a passive construction.
  • Option 4 (D) 'No error' is incorrect because there is an error in segment C.

questionText:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
We have to say little in this matter.

options.text: Little had to be said in this matter.
In this matter, little is to be said.
In this matter, little must be said.
Little has to be said in this matter.

solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is Option 4.
Key Points
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
  • In the active voice, the sentence is: "We have to say little in this matter."
  • To convert to passive voice: Place the object "little" at the beginning.
  • Change the active verb form "have to say" to "has to be said" (passive form).
  • Ensure the phrase "in this matter" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
Correct Sentence: "Little has to be said in this matter."
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "Little had to be said in this matter." – Incorrect tense (past tense).
  • Option 2: "In this matter, little is to be said." – Incorrect structure and verb form.
  • Option 3: "In this matter, little must be said." – Incorrect modal verb usage.

questionText:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. But a dove that happened to be sitting on a neighbouring tree saw the ant's danger and, plucking off a leaf, let it drop into the water before him.

B. Just at that time, a fowler was spreading his net and was in the act of ensnaring the dove, when the ant, perceiving his object, bit his heel.

C. An ant went to a fountain to quench his thirst and, tumbling in, almost drowned.

D. The ant mounting upon it, was presently wafted safely ashore.
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is option 3) i.e., 'CADB'.
Key Points
  • When arranging sentences, it is easier to order the first few; and then eliminate the options accordingly.
  • The first sentence of a paragraph is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it.
  • Here, only C is independent and introduces the subject of the passage which deals with an ant which almost drowned.
  • It should be followed by A which moves the story forward by talking about how a dove saw the ant in danger and what action the dove took.
  • So, A must come after C. Then CA is the correct order.
  • This order is only shown in option 3, which shows the full sequence as: CADB.

Thus, the correct sequence is: CADB

C. An ant went to a fountain to quench his thirst and, tumbling in, almost drowned.

A. But a dove that happened to be sitting on a neighbouring tree saw the ant's danger and, plucking off a leaf, let it drop into the water before him.

D. The ant mounting upon it, was presently wafted safely ashore.

B. Just at that time, a fowler was spreading his net and was in the act of ensnaring the dove, when the ant, perceiving his object, bit his heel.

questionText:
In the following question, choose the word which is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Colossal
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is 'Small.'

Key Points

  • Colossal means 'extremely large (अतिविशाल, वृहत्‍काय, बहुत बड़ा)'.
    • ​Example: Companies today are highly competitive and welcome the colossal saving of time and money by introducing new methods.
  • Marked option 'Small' means 'not large in size, number, amount, etc. (छोटा आकार, संख्‍या, मात्रा आदि की दृष्टि से)'.
    • ​Example: Small businesses are the lifeblood of the economy.
  • It is clear that Colossal and 'Small' are opposite in meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is option 3.

Additional Information

  • Giant means something that is very large (बहुत बड़े आकार की कोई वस्‍तु; भीमकाय).
  • Dark means with no light or very little light (अँधेरा, काला-सा, साँवला).
  • Opaque means something that one cannot see through (ऐसा कुछ जिसे कोई देख नहीं सकता; अपारदर्शी).

questionText:
In the following question, the given sentence has four parts marked as A, B, C, and D. Choose the part of the sentence with an error and mark it as your answer. If there is no error, mark D as your answer.

My senior asked me (A) / whether I was interested (B) / to joining the group for the skit. (C) / No Error (D)
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is A

Key Points

  • Part C of the sentence is erroneous.
  • To- infinitive is used as 'to + base form of the verb' example to dance, to play, to sing, etc.
  • Since to-infinitive is used in the sentence, the verb 'joining' should be replaced with 'join'.

​Hence, the correct sentence would be, My senior asked me whether I was interested to join the group for the skit.

Therefore, it can be inferred that the correct answer is option 3)

Additional Information

There are certain verbs used in the following pattern: Subject + Verb + Past Participle(-ing form of the verb)

  • Some of the verbs are: hate, stop, finish, enjoy, etc.
    • ​Ex: He hates coming late to the company.

questionText:
Read the sentence to find out whether there is any grammatical error in it. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. Spot the error from the given options.

The students of (a)/ commerce stream are (b)/ not able to cope up (c)/ with the new syllabus (d).
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is 'c.'

Key Points

  • The error lies in part (c) of the sentence.
  • “Cope up with” is an incorrect structure.
  • 'Cope with' means to deal successfully with a difficult situation or job.
    • Example: It must be really hard to cope with three young children and a job.
  • “Cope up” is an interpretation that is sometimes used incorrectly in place of “keep up.”
  • Hence, 'cope up' should be replaced by '​cope' to make the sentence grammatically correct.
  • ​Correct Sentence: The students of commerce stream are not able to cope with the new syllabus.


Additional Information

  • A conjunction is a joiner, a word that connects (conjoins) parts of a sentence.
  • Coordinating conjunctions join equals to one another.
    • Example: Most children like sweets and cookies.
  • Coordinating conjunctions go in between items joined, not at the beginning or end.
    • Example: I like coffee, but I don't like tea.

Hinglish

  • त्रुटि वाक्य के भाग (c) में निहित है।
  • “Cope up with” एक गलत संरचना है।
  • “Cope with” का अर्थ है किसी कठिन परिस्थिति या नौकरी से सफलतापूर्वक निपटना।
    • Example: It must be really hard to cope with three young children and a job.
  • "Cope up" एक व्याख्या है जिसे कभी-कभी "keep up" के स्थान पर गलत तरीके से उपयोग किया जाता है।
  • इसलिए, वाक्य को व्याकरणिक रूप से सही बनाने के लिए cope up को ​cope द्वारा प्रतिस्थापित किया जाना चाहिए।

questionText:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

If I go to Bangalore, I ______with my nephew.
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is Option 2)

Key Points

  • The given sentence is a first conditional sentence, which describes a probable future event and its result.
  • In first conditional sentences, the structure is
    • if + present simple + will + base form of the verb.
  • We use the present simple tense in the if-clause (If I go) and "will" plus the base form of the verb in the main clause (I will stay).

Hence, the correct statement is 'If I go to Bangalore, I will stay with my nephew.'

Additional Information

  • The first conditional is used to talk about real or possible future situations and their likely outcomes.
  • Other structures fit different types of conditionals: second conditional uses "if + past simple, would + base form" for hypothetical situations
  • Third conditional uses "if + past perfect, would have + past participle" for hypothetical situations in the past.

questionText:
Direction: Spot the erroneous parts, if any, in the following sentences:

a) COVID 19 is a disease / (b) that effects / (c) mainly older people./ (d) No error.
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is '(b)'.

Key Points

  • The error lies in Part (b) of the sentence.
  • The meaning of the noun 'effect' is the result of a particular influence.
    • ​​Example: I tried taking tablets for the headache but they didn't have any effect.
  • ​The meaning of the verb 'affect' is to have an influence on someone or something or to cause a change in someone or something.
    • Example: Both buildings were badly affected by the fire.
  • In the above given sentence, the disease has an influence on old people.
  • ​Therefore, the use of 'effects' in Part (b) of the sentence should be replaced by 'affects' to make it grammatically correct.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is '(b)'.

​Correct sentence: COVID 19 is a disease that affects mainly older people.

questionText:
In the following items, each passage consists of six sentences. The first sentence (S1) and the final sentence (S6) are given. The middle four sentences in each have been removed and jumbled up. These are labelled P, Q, R and S. You are required to find out the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

S1: Happiness, after all, is an inner state of mind.
P: Some of the most miserable persons I have come across in my life are rich.
Q: It is little dependent on outside environment.
​R: Happiness has very little to do, for instance, with whether you are rich or not rich.
S: It is true that poverty makes one miserable in a very acute way.
S6: My point is that it is not wealth but coordination of one's thought and action which removes inner conflicts.
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is "QRSP"

Key Points

  • Sentence S1 introduces the idea that happiness is an inner state of mind that is not dependent on external factors.
  • Sentence Q further emphasizes this point by stating that happiness has very little to do with whether a person is rich or not.
  • Sentence R and S add that some of the most miserable people are actually rich, indicating that wealth is not a guarantee of happiness.
  • Sentence P mentions that poverty can make a person miserable in a very acute way, but this is not the main focus of the passage.
  • Finally, sentence S6 concludes the paragraph by stating that it is the coordination of one's thoughts and actions that leads to a lack of inner conflicts and ultimately to happiness.
  • When the sentences are put in this order, they form a coherent and logical paragraph about the relationship between happiness and wealth.

Thus, option 4 is the correct answer.

Correct paragraph: S1 Happiness, after all, is an inner state of mind. Q It is little dependent on outside environment. R Happiness has very little to do, for instance, with whether you are rich or not rich. S It is true that poverty makes one miserable in a very acute way. P Some of the most miserable persons I have come across in my life are rich. S6 My point is that it is not wealth but coordination of one's thought and action which removes inner conflicts.

questionText:
In the following question, there is a related pair of words given. Each pair is followed by four other pairs of words. Choose the pair from the given option the pair of words that best expresses the relationship like the original pair.

Shame​: Honor
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is '​Cautious: ​Hasty​.'

Key Points

  • Let us see the meanings of the words given in the question- Shame: Honor​​:
    • Shame: the unpleasant feeling of guilt and embarrassment that you get when you have done something stupid or morally wrong; the ability to have this feeling. (लज्‍जा, शर्म (मूर्खतापूर्ण या अनैतिक काम से उत्‍पन्‍न अपराध और व्‍याकुलता की भावना); लज्‍जाशीलता, शरमीलापन)
    • Honor: the respect from other people that a person, country, etc. gets because of high standards of behaviour and moral character. (आदर, सम्‍मान)
  • In the given pair Shame: Honor​​, the antonym of 'Shame' is 'Honor'.
  • Now, let us explore the meanings of the words from the option:
    • Hypocrisy: behaviour in which somebody pretends to have moral standards or opinions that he/she does not really have. ((वास्‍तविकता के विपरीत) उच्‍च नैतिक मानदंड और व्‍यवहार का ढोंग रचना; पाखंड, ढोंग, मिथ्‍याचार)
    • Deception: making somebody believe or being made to believe something that is not true. (धोखा देने की क्रिया)
    • Daring: adventurous or audaciously bold. (साहसी या दुस्साहसी बोल्ड)
    • Courageous: not deterred by danger or pain; brave. (खतरे या दर्द से विचलित नहीं; बहादुर)
    • Cautious​​: taking great care to avoid possible danger or problems. (सावधान, सतर्क, चौकस)
    • Hasty: said or done too quickly. (जल्‍दी में कहा या किया हुआ; तीव्र गतिक)

questionText:
The following question consists of an incomplete sentence or a sentence which is split into four parts. All four parts are jumbled up and are named as P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Arrange the jumbled parts of the sentence and find out which of the four combinations from the given options will correctly complete the sentence.

Le Corbusier was born in a small town____________. All his life he was marked by the harshness of these surroundings and the puritanism of a Protestant environment.

P) in the mountainous Swiss Jura region
Q) since the 18th century the
R) world's center of
S) precision watchmaking.
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is PQRS.

Key Points

  • The given question is an example of sentence rearrangement.
  • The first sentence should begin with Segment P as it tells the information about the Subject (Le Corbusier's birthplace).
  • Moreover, The next sentence has two clauses that segments Q and R are connected to each other.
  • If we read carefully, Segment Q is starting with time denoting the word 'since' and ends with an article 'the' which we use before the definite article noun (ie. world).
  • Thus, Segment Q is connected with R.
  • Out of the given options, only option 1 contains Segment P as the starting segment, thereby, making it the correct answer.

Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 1.

Important Points

  • Important Rules to Solve the sentence rearrangements:
    • Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
    • Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).
    • Try to identify the mandatory pairs.
    • Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.

Many people are born crying, live complaining and die disappointed. They think every other person's burden to be light and their own feathers to be heavy as lead, and yet if the truth were known, it is their fancy rather than their fate that makes things go so hard with them. Without patience wisdom cannot be used properly.

Therefore the correct answer is option 4.

questionText: Comprehension: Direction: Read the passage given below and answer the questions that follow by selecting the correct/most appropriate options. Good nutrition has the power to empower the present and future generations. India's greatest national treasure is its people - especially women and children - but even after 75 years of independence a majority of them do not get the required diet to meet their nutritional needs. A child's nutritional status is directly linked to their mother. Poor nutrition among pregnant women affects the nutritional status of the child and has a greater chance to affect future generations. Under-nourished children are at risk of under-performing in studies and have limited job prospects. This vicious cycle restrains the development of the country, whose work-force, affected mentally and physically, has reduced work capacity. While there has been some progress in tackling malnutrition among children and women over the past decade, the improvement has been modest at best. This is despite declining rates of poverty, increased self-sufficiency in food production, and the implementation of a range of government programs. The National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) has shown marginal improvement in different nutrition indicators such as Stunting, Wasting and Anemia, indicating that the pace of progress is slow. Children in several States are more undernourished now than they were five years ago. There is a greater need now to increase investment in women and children's health and nutrition to ensure their sustainable development and improved quality of life. While the Government's focus has been on the consolidation of several programmes to improve outcomes, there is a need for increased financial commitment. Experts have pointed out that Saksham Angandwadi and the Prime Minister's Overarching Scheme for Holistic Nourishment (POSHAN) 2.0 programme have seen only a marginal increase in budgetary allocation this year (Rs. 20,263 crore from Rs. 20,105 crore in 2021-22). Additionally, 32% of funds released under POSHAN Abhiyaan to States and Union Territories have not been utilised.
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is 'Poor nutrition among pregnant women'.

Key Points

  • The given passage is all about 'Malnutrition among Children and Women'.
  • The first paragraph says "Poor nutrition among pregnant women affects the nutritional status of the child and has a greater chance to affect future generations".
  • From the above line, we can clearly say that poor nutrition among pregnant women affects their nutritional status.

Hence, the only possible answer is 'option 3'.

questionText: Direction: Read the following passage carefully and answer the question given below it. As the rulers of the planet, human beings like to think that it is the large creatures who will emerge victorious in the struggle for survival. However, nature teaches us the opposite. It is often the smallest species which are the toughest and most adaptable. A perfect example is the hummingbird, which is found in the American countries. One species of hummingbird is known as the bee hummingbird which ranks as the world's smallest and lightest bird and it is barely visible when it is in flight. Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards. They feed mainly on the nectar of flowers, a liquid that is rich in energy. Nectar is an ideal food source, for hummingbirds need an incredible amount of energy to sustain their body metabolism. A hummingbird's wings flap at a rate of about 80 times per second and its tiny heart beats more than 1000 times per minute. This is why they must consume relatively large quantities of food. In the course of a day, a hummingbird consumes nectar as much as half its body weight. The beauty of Nature is the uniqueness of her creation to adapt in any condition.

It escapes our sight when it is in flight
It can fly high beyond the clouds

solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is 'It escapes our sight when it is in flight​.'
